verdict: Avoid new pharma/API exposure in Panaji: Goa's local demand signals are weak and the national data call is Avoid, so lend only to the strongest formulation-led borrowers with tight structure, and decline API-only units.
title: Panaji Pharmaceuticals & APIs: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**A pharma or API unit here buys raw materials and solvents, runs them through reactors and formulation lines, and sells to formulators, exporters or institutions.** Cash is made on yield per batch and on the spread between input cost and the contract price; value sits in the customer approval and the dossier, not the plant. **Working capital is the real business: receivables and inventory eat cash long before the sale converts.** Rating reports show this plainly — Concord Biotech's working capital intensity ran 52% in FY2019, 47% in FY2020 and 48% in 7MFY2021 [8], and Cohance Lifesciences carried term loans of Rs. 152 crore against operating cash flow of Rs. 200 crore in FY24 [7]. So when a proposal lands, check the receivables and inventory days first; if the working capital intensity is near half of sales, ask what the customer mix is and whether any single buyer crosses a third of revenue.

## What has changed now
**The local economy is running behind the country, and that is the fact that decides this note.** Goa's GST collections are -1.2% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1%, 7.3 pp slower [D], and electricity demand is +6.7% against India's +9.5%, 2.8 pp slower [D]. Nationally, output is -2.1% Apr-to-date while bank credit is +21.6% YoY, a gap of +23.7 pp [D] — money is being lent faster than goods are being made. **The data call is Avoid at 16, and the local signals do not soften it.** Note the sources say almost nothing specific about Panaji's pharma cluster; the local directory [1] is undated and carries no financials, so lean on first principles and the peer set.

## Where the growth is
**Peer results are strong and that is where to hunt, not in the local stress.** Aarti Pharmalabs reported record quarterly revenue of Rs. 613 crore, up 47% YoY, with EBITDA of Rs. 136 crore and margin at 22.2% from 17.7% [2][4]. RPG Life Sciences grew revenue 16.5% to Rs. 211.6 crore and targets 25% API growth with another acquisition within 12 months [3][5]. **Pursue formulation-led units with an approved customer base and CDMO or export contracts; avoid pure API traders and single-customer contract research shops.** The ICRA rating on one small player shows revenue of Rs. 61.0 crore in FY2024 with high customer concentration [6] — that is the profile to decline.

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the working-capital cycle, not the plant.** Take monthly stock and receivable statements, a monthly GST return, and quarterly financials; covenant a minimum current ratio and a cap on single-customer concentration. **Price for the receivables risk and keep tenor short.** Where capex is planned, ask for the customer contract backing it before sanction; if there is none, decline. Collect from customer the actual receivable days, inventory days and customer-wise sales split — the sources give none for this city.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the customer, not the factory.** A fall in monthly GST turnover, a jump in receivable days, or a top buyer cutting orders are the first signals; act on the first, not the third.
watch: Turnover falls two months running -> freeze fresh limits and review drawing power
Receivable days rise beyond the sanctioned norm -> ask for customer-wise ageing and cut limit
Single buyer crosses a third of sales -> seek diversification plan or reduce exposure
Usage drops while sales are flat -> verify stock build-up and inspect godown
